=== vault-schema.md
# Vault schema (wiki-master)

This vault is an LLM-maintained wiki (Karpathy pattern). Maintained by the
`wiki-master` Claude Code plugin.

## Layout
- `raw/` — captured sources. The **content is never modified**: no LLM rewriting, no
  reinterpreting what a source said — that integrity is the whole point of provenance.
  Deterministic tooling may still perform *faithful* representation transforms that preserve
  the content — text extraction, localizing an image reference to a stored copy, pipeline-state
  frontmatter. The line is semantic (never alter the evidence), not byte-level (freeze the file).
  `raw/clippings/` — Web Clipper / clip.mjs output. `raw/attachments/` — downloaded assets,
  content-hash named.
- `wiki/sources|entities|concepts|syntheses|authored` — LLM-owned pages. Under
  `wiki/authored/`, a page belonging to a multi-doc project lives at
  `wiki/authored/<project>/[<subproject>/]<file>.md` — see the Frontmatter contract
  below for the `project`/`kind` fields that drive this, and
  `skills/wiki-user/references/authoring.md` for the canonical per-kind placement table
  ("write a user guide" always resolves to `<project>/guides/user.md`, etc.).
- `moc/` — Maps of Content. `index.md` — catalog. `log/` — one file per operation, viewed via `log.base`.
- `.recycle/` — purged topics, one folder per purge with a `manifest.json` recording what
  moved (by path and by `source-hash`) and which source URLs were declined. Git-tracked, so a
  removal reaches every machine; dot-prefixed, so no search, metric or graph walk ever sees it.
  Never emptied automatically — a purge is reversible, and that is what makes it safe to run.

## Frontmatter contract
- Raw/clippings: `title, source, author, published, created, tags:[clippings], quality, topic, source-hash`.
  `topic` records the research topic the clipping was gathered for (the argument given to
  `wiki-researcher` discovery); it is omitted for clips made outside a research run, and it is what the
  triage queue groups by.
- Wiki pages: `type, created, updated, reviewed, status, sources:["[[...]]"], ai-generated`.
  Source pages also carry `source-hashes:[<sha256>,…]` — the `source-hash` of each
  clipping they summarize; this is the content key the ingest-backlog metric joins on.
  `wiki/authored/` pages additionally carry optional `project` (a slug, one `/` deep
  at most for a sub-project) and `kind` (`overview|architecture|reference|guide|
  diagram|decision|roadmap|note|backlog-item`) — grouping metadata a per-project MOC
  generator reads; a `kind: decision` page also carries `decision-status`
  (`proposed|accepted|superseded|deprecated`), and a `kind: backlog-item` page
  carries `backlog-status` (`planned|in-progress|shipped|blocked|dropped`) — one
  small file per tracked item, edited in place as status changes rather than
  accumulating appended "Update (date): ..." paragraphs. A backlog item may also
  carry `depends-on`, a list of quoted wikilinks to other backlog items of the same
  project; it never changes the item's own status.

## Rules

### Identity, relationships and verification

Concepts may carry `aliases: ["equivalent name"]` and a one-sentence `scope:`.
Search existing titles/aliases and neighboring concepts before creating a new one.
Different scopes remain distinct pages; aliases do not mean broader or related.
Use full-path links whenever a basename or alias is ambiguous.

Keep supporting citations in `sources:` and factual prose. Put navigation in
`## Relationships` or `Related:`, with an explanatory sentence and a small role
vocabulary: broader, narrower, prerequisite, complements, alternative, contrasts,
applies-to. Navigation does not make the destination supporting evidence.

`reviewed` records factual verification. `updated` records edits. Mechanical
changes preserve `reviewed`; missing review means unverified. Index freshness
is a third, independent state. MOCs route tasks through prerequisites, alternatives,
complementary topics and evidence; generated project catalogs are separate from
curated task maps. See `_templates/concept-note.md` and `_templates/task-map.md`.
- Raw is the source of truth. Every wiki page cites its `raw/` provenance —
  **except** `wiki/authored/`: original, primary content (advisory documentation,
  policy, house style) written directly into the wiki, not derived from a
  captured source. These pages declare the exception explicitly (`sources: []`)
  rather than by omission; they are living pages like any other `wiki/` page,
  never requiring a `raw/` counterpart.
- Links are `[[wikilinks]]`; embeds `![[...]]` are transclusion only.

## Git ownership

The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit` commits what one
operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. Obsidian Git stays installed for its
source-control view and for pulling, with auto-commit, commit on file change and auto-push
all off. An instruction anywhere else that says otherwise is stale.

The deployed relay persists messages in a local queue and dispatches them using one worker. A second worker is proposed, not implemented.

content.content:
=== op-begin
usage: node scripts/op-begin.mjs --op <op>

Opens a vault operation: records what is already uncommitted and prints the token that op-commit takes as --since.
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).
=== op-commit
usage: node scripts/op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token> [--paths-file <JSON-file>] [--include <path>]... [--include-from <JSON-file>] [--evidence-map <JSON-file>]

Commits one operation's changes and closes its token. With --paths-file only the ledger's paths are committed; a ledger path that was already uncommitted when the operation opened is refused unless --include (or --include-from) adopts it. Never pushes.
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).
=== log-entry
usage: node scripts/log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>" [--since <token>]   (entry body on stdin)

Writes one uniquely named log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md. Write it after op-begin and list it in the operation's ledger: --since records its path there (op-ledger.mjs show prints the ledger).
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).
=== refresh-catalogs
usage: node scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs [--project <slug>] [--apply] [--paths-file <ledger>] [--diff] [--since <token>]

Regenerates a project's roadmap catalog, project map and the global index from one vault graph.
The default is a dry run whose "changed" list is what an apply would change; --diff adds the lines each file would lose and gain on stderr. --paths-file is the operation's ownership ledger: another writer's uncommitted pages stay out. With --apply, --since records the changed paths in the operation's written-paths ledger (op-ledger.mjs show prints it).
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).

usage: node scripts/validate-authored.mjs --paths-file <ledger.json> [--json] [--terms-file <file>] [--terms-projects <list>]

Checks the frontmatter, placement and links of exactly the pages one authoring task wrote (the ledger: a JSON array of vault-relative paths). Prints one "path:line rule message" line per defect; exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects, 2 an unusable ledger or vault.
Read-only.

Dry run: prints what it would change. Add --apply to write.

=== index-gen
usage: node scripts/index-gen.mjs [--paths-file <JSON array>] [--since <token>]

Regenerates the catalog between the fence markers of index.md. Manual framing outside the fence is kept.
Without an option it lists every page on disk, another writer's uncommitted pages included.
--paths-file <JSON array of vault-relative paths> is the operation's ownership ledger: the catalog then lists a page only when it is in
the last commit or the ledger names it, and keeps a line it already holds for another writer's page that still exists.
--since <token> records index.md in the operation's written-paths ledger when the file changed (op-ledger.mjs show prints the ledger).
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).
=== wiki-sync
usage: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs [--commit-local | --op <token> [--paths-file <ledger.json>] [--title "<title>"]]

Brings the vault and its shared remote to the same state: rebases onto the upstream, pushes, and checks the remote has the commits, or says exactly why it could not. --commit-local first commits the vault's uncommitted changes itself; it refuses while an operation is open.
--op <token> first closes that one operation (the close op-commit makes: scoped by --paths-file, else by the paths its writers recorded, else unscoped, which is refused while another operation is open), then syncs and verifies. A refused close prints "not committed:" and pushes nothing; a close that landed but could not be published prints "committed, not published:". --op cannot be combined with --commit-local.
The vault is the one named by WIKI_MASTER_VAULT (default: ~/.wiki-master-vault).

# Beacon architecture

## As built (deployed relay)

- **Queue persistence:** the relay persists each message in a local queue before it acknowledges the message.
- **Dispatch:** a single dispatcher worker drains the queue and dispatches messages.

## Planned, not implemented

A second dispatcher worker is proposed, not built. The proposal, its acceptance criteria and the benchmark gate are tracked in [[wiki/authored/beacon/backlog/parallel-workers.md]]. Nothing in the as-built section above changes until that item ships.

backlog-status: planned
---
# Parallel workers

Not shipped. The deployed relay runs one dispatcher worker; see [[wiki/authored/beacon/architecture.md]] for the as-built behavior.

## Proposal

Run two dispatcher workers against the relay's local queue instead of one. This is a design proposal only.

## Acceptance criteria

- Messages that share a key are dispatched in the order they were enqueued, even with two workers running.
- Each message is still persisted to the local queue before it is acknowledged, as today.

## Requirement before shipping

Benchmark the two-worker design against the current one-worker relay before it ships, and ship only if the benchmark supports it.
EOF
